source.text: Παρακαλῶ οὖν πρῶτον πάντων ποιεῖσθαι δεήσεις, προσευχάς, ἐντεύξεις, εὐχαριστίας, ὑπὲρ πάντων ἀνθρώπων, ὑπὲρ βασιλέων καὶ πάντων τῶν ἐν ὑπεροχῇ ὄντων, ἵνα ἤρεμον καὶ ἡσύχιον βίον διάγωμεν ἐν πάσῃ εὐσεβείᾳ καὶ σεμνότητι.

records.literal_gloss: I urge therefore first of all to be made requests, prayers, intercessions, thanksgivings for all men, \v 2 for kings and all those in high position being, so that a quiet and peaceful life we may lead in all godliness and dignity.

en.L: First of all, then, I urge that requests, prayers, intercessions [and] thanksgivings be made for {{gender:all people|all men}}, \v 2 for kings and all who are in high positions, so that we may lead a quiet and peaceful life in all godliness and dignity.
en.B: First of all, then, I urge that requests, prayers, intercessions and thanks be offered for {{gender:everyone|all men}}: \v 2 for kings and for all who hold high office, so that we may live peaceful and quiet lives, fully devoted to God and worthy of respect.
en.R: First, I ask you to pray for everyone. Ask God to help them, pray for them, speak to God for them, and thank God for them. \v 2 Pray for kings and for everyone who has power over others, so that we can live in peace and quiet, honoring God and living good lives.

fr.L: J’exhorte donc, avant tout, à faire des demandes, des prières, des intercessions, des actions de grâces pour {{gender:tous les humains|tous les hommes}}, \v 2 pour les rois et tous ceux qui sont en position d’autorité, afin que nous menions une vie calme et paisible en toute piété et dignité.
fr.B: Avant tout, donc, je demande qu’on présente à Dieu des demandes, des prières, des intercessions et des remerciements pour {{gender:tous les êtres humains|tous les hommes}} : \v 2 pour les rois et pour tous ceux qui exercent l’autorité, afin que nous puissions mener une vie paisible et tranquille, entièrement attachés à Dieu et dignes de respect.
fr.R: Tout d’abord, il faut prier pour tout le monde. Il faut demander à Dieu de les aider, prier pour eux, parler à Dieu en leur faveur, et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} remercier pour eux. \v 2 Il faut prier pour les rois et pour tous ceux qui ont du pouvoir sur les autres, afin que nous puissions vivre dans la paix et le calme, en honorant Dieu et en menant une vie bonne.

decisions.choice: requests, prayers, intercessions, thanksgivings
decisions.reason: The four words overlap and together cover every kind of prayer. ἐντεύξεις is prayer on behalf of others.

decisions.choice: for all people
decisions.reason: ἀνθρώπων is the general word for human beings. "All people" is a theme of the passage (verses 4, 6).

decisions.choice: kings and all in high positions: the emperor and the authorities
decisions.reason: In Paul's world "the king" was the Roman emperor (1 Peter 2:13-17). Jews prayed for the rulers of the nations they lived among (Jeremiah 29:7).

decisions.choice: godliness: devotion to God shown in life
decisions.reason: εὐσεβείᾳ is a key word of these letters (3:16; 4:7-8; 6:6): reverence for God that shapes how one lives.

decisions.choice: {{gender:all people|all men}} (L); {{gender:everyone|all men}} (B)
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general (m2); "men" is the traditional form.

decisions.choice: Ask God to help them, pray for them, speak to God for them, and thank God for them
decisions.reason: Readable turns the four nouns into actions (m1).

decisions.choice: {{gender:tous les humains|tous les hommes}} (L); {{gender:tous les êtres humains|tous les hommes}} (B); "tout le monde" with no span (R)
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general (m2). Balanced does not follow the English "everyone" with "tout le monde", because in verse 4 the same phrase governs a verb, and "tout le monde soit sauvé" (singular) and "tous les hommes soient sauvés" (plural) would not agree; a plural noun keeps both options correct. Readable's "tout le monde" is already inclusive and needs no setting.

decisions.choice: "il faut prier" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek names no one: Paul urges that prayers be made, by the church that Timothy leads. French would have to choose between "tu" (Timothy alone) and "vous" (the church) for the English "you"; the impersonal form keeps the instruction open, as the Greek does.

source.text: τοῦτο καλὸν καὶ ἀπόδεκτον ἐνώπιον τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν θεοῦ, ὃς πάντας ἀνθρώπους θέλει σωθῆναι καὶ εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν ἀληθείας ἐλθεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: This [is] good and acceptable before the Savior of us God, \v 4 who all men wants to be saved and to [the] knowledge of [the] truth to come.

en.L: This [is] good and pleasing before God our Savior, \v 4 who wants {{gender:all people|all men}} to be saved and to come to [the] knowledge of [the] truth.
en.B: This is good, and it pleases God our Savior, \v 4 who wants {{gender:everyone|all men}} to be saved and to come to know the truth.
en.R: This is good, and it pleases God our Savior. \v 4 God wants all people to be saved and to know the truth.

fr.L: Cela [est] bon et agréable devant Dieu notre Sauveur, \v 4 qui veut que {{gender:tous les humains|tous les hommes}} soient sauvés et parviennent à la connaissance de la vérité.
fr.B: Cela est bon, et c’est agréable à Dieu notre Sauveur, \v 4 qui veut que {{gender:tous les êtres humains|tous les hommes}} soient sauvés et arrivent à connaître la vérité.
fr.R: C’est une bonne chose, et cela plaît à Dieu notre Sauveur. \v 4 Dieu veut que tous les gens soient sauvés et connaissent la vérité.

decisions.choice: God wants all people to be saved
decisions.reason: θέλω expresses God's desire. Because God wants all to be saved, prayer is for all (verse 1). Paul does not here discuss how God's desire relates to those who refuse it.

decisions.choice: the knowledge of the truth: coming to know the gospel
decisions.reason: ἐπίγνωσιν is real, personal knowledge (Colossians 1:9). "The truth" is the gospel (2 Timothy 2:25; Titus 1:1).

decisions.choice: {{gender:all people|all men}} (L); {{gender:everyone|all men}} (B)
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

source.text: εἷς γὰρ θεός, εἷς καὶ μεσίτης θεοῦ καὶ ἀνθρώπων ἄνθρωπος Χριστὸς Ἰησοῦς, ὁ δοὺς ἑαυτὸν ἀντίλυτρον ὑπὲρ πάντων, τὸ μαρτύριον καιροῖς ἰδίοις·

records.literal_gloss: One for God, one also mediator of God and men, a man Christ Jesus, \v 6 the [one] having given himself [as] a ransom for all, the testimony in its own times;

en.L: For [there is] one God, and one mediator between God and {{gender:humankind|men}}, the man {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, \v 6 who gave {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} [as] a ransom for all, the testimony [given] at the proper time.
en.B: For there is one God, and one mediator between God and humanity, {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} human, \v 6 who gave {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} as a ransom for all. This was the testimony given at the right time.
en.R: There is only one God. And there is only one who can bring God and people together. He is {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, who became a human being. \v 6 He gave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life to pay the price that would set all people free. God showed us this at the right time.

fr.L: Car [il y a] un seul Dieu, et un seul médiateur entre Dieu et {{gender:les humains|les hommes}}, un homme, le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus, \v 6 qui s’est donné {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} en rançon pour tous, le témoignage [rendu] au temps fixé.
fr.B: Car il y a un seul Dieu, et un seul médiateur entre Dieu et l’humanité, le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus, homme {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, \v 6 qui s’est donné {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} en rançon pour tous. C’est là le témoignage rendu au moment voulu.
fr.R: Il n’y a qu’un seul Dieu. Et il n’y a qu’un seul médiateur qui peut réunir Dieu et les humains : c’est le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus, qui est devenu un être humain. \v 6 Il a donné {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} vie pour payer le prix qui libère tous les humains. Dieu nous l’a montré au moment voulu.

decisions.choice: one God: the confession of Israel
decisions.reason: "The LORD our God, the LORD is one" (Deuteronomy 6:4). Because there is one God of all, there is one way to him for all (Romans 3:29-30).

decisions.choice: mediator: one who stands between two parties to bring them together
decisions.reason: μεσίτης is a go-between. Moses is called a mediator in Galatians 3:19-20; here Christ alone fills that role.

decisions.choice: a man, Christ Jesus: himself a human being
decisions.reason: ἄνθρωπος is the general word for a human being. The point is that the mediator shares the humanity of those he brings to God.

decisions.choice: gave himself as a ransom for all: the saying of Jesus in Mark 10:45
decisions.reason: Jesus said he came "to give his life as a ransom for many" (Mark 10:45). ἀντίλυτρον is a strengthened form of the word for ransom, the price paid to set captives free. "For all" picks up verses 1 and 4.

decisions.choice: the testimony at the proper time: Christ's self-giving is God's witness, given when the time had come
decisions.reason: The phrase stands loosely in the sentence: the giving of Christ is the testimony God bore, at the time God chose (Galatians 4:4; Titus 1:3).

decisions.choice: humankind (L); humanity (B); people (R); the man (L); himself human (B); who became a human being (R)
decisions.reason: ἀνθρώπων means human beings in general; Literal offers "men" as the traditional form. ἄνθρωπος stresses that Christ is human (m3).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: gave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life to pay the price that would set all people free
alternatives: gave himself as a ransom for all
decisions.reason: Readable explains "ransom" (m4).

decisions.choice: {{gender:les humains|les hommes}} ... un homme (L)
decisions.reason: As in English, the first word means human beings in general and Literal offers "les hommes" as the traditional form; the second is said of Christ, who was a man, so "un homme" takes no setting. The traditional option keeps the echo of the Greek ("les hommes, un homme"); the default keeps the sense.

source.text: εἰς ὃ ἐτέθην ἐγὼ κῆρυξ καὶ ἀπόστολος ἀλήθειαν λέγω, οὐ ψεύδομαι διδάσκαλος ἐθνῶν ἐν πίστει καὶ ἀληθείᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: for which was appointed I a herald and apostle, truth I speak, not I lie, a teacher of Gentiles in faith and truth.

en.L: For this I was appointed a herald and an apostle (I am telling the truth, I am not lying), a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
en.B: For this purpose I was appointed a preacher and an apostle (I am telling the truth; I am not lying), a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
en.R: God chose me to tell this good news and to be an apostle. I am telling you the truth. I am not lying. God made me a teacher of people who are not Jews, to teach them about faith and the truth.

fr.L: Pour cela, moi, j’ai été établi héraut et apôtre (je dis la vérité, je ne mens pas), enseignant des nations dans la foi et la vérité.
fr.B: C’est pour cela que j’ai été établi prédicateur et apôtre (je dis la vérité, je ne mens pas), enseignant des non-Juifs dans la foi et la vérité.
fr.R: Dieu m’a choisi pour annoncer cette bonne nouvelle et pour être apôtre. Je te dis la vérité. Je ne mens pas. Dieu a fait de moi celui qui enseigne les gens qui ne sont pas juifs, pour leur faire connaître la foi et la vérité.

decisions.choice: herald: one who announces a public message
decisions.reason: κῆρυξ was the public crier who announced a ruler's decrees.

decisions.choice: I am telling the truth, I am not lying: a solemn assurance
decisions.reason: The same oath-like words are in Romans 9:1. Paul's mission to the Gentiles was questioned by some.

decisions.choice: in faith and truth: faithfully and truly, or about faith and truth
decisions.reason: ἐν πίστει καὶ ἀληθείᾳ may describe how he teaches or what he teaches; the sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: preacher
decisions.reason: "Herald" is now unfamiliar; the sense is one who proclaims (m1).

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable explains "Gentiles".

decisions.choice: les nations (L); les non-Juifs (B); les gens qui ne sont pas juifs (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for the New Testament: "les Gentils" is no longer current French and "les païens" sounds pejorative today. Literal keeps the biblical "les nations"; Balanced and Readable say who is meant, as the English "Gentiles" and "people who are not Jews" do.

source.text: Βούλομαι οὖν προσεύχεσθαι τοὺς ἄνδρας ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ, ἐπαίροντας ὁσίους χεῖρας χωρὶς ὀργῆς καὶ διαλογισμοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: I want therefore to pray the men in every place, lifting up holy hands without anger and argument.

en.L: Therefore I want the men to pray in every place, lifting up holy hands without anger or argument.
en.B: So I want the men everywhere to pray, lifting up holy hands, free from anger and quarreling.
en.R: So I want the men in every place where you meet to pray. When they lift up their hands to God, their lives should be holy, and they should not be angry or arguing with each other.

fr.L: Je veux donc que les hommes prient en tout lieu, en élevant des mains saintes, sans colère ni dispute.
fr.B: Je veux donc que, partout, les hommes prient en levant des mains saintes, sans colère ni querelles.
fr.R: Je veux donc que, partout où vous vous réunissez, les hommes prient. Quand ils lèvent les mains vers Dieu, leur vie doit être sainte, et ils ne doivent pas être en colère ni se disputer entre eux.

decisions.choice: the men: the male members, as distinct from the women of verse 9
decisions.reason: ἄνδρας is the word for males (or husbands), not the general word for people used in verses 1-6. Paul addresses the men first, then the women.

decisions.choice: in every place: wherever the church gathers
decisions.reason: Probably every house where believers met in and around Ephesus (compare 1 Corinthians 1:2).

decisions.choice: lifting up holy hands: the ordinary posture of prayer
decisions.reason: Jews and Christians commonly prayed standing with hands raised (1 Kings 8:22; Psalm 141:2). "Holy" hands are hands not stained by wrongdoing.

decisions.choice: in every place where you meet; their lives should be holy
decisions.reason: Readable says what "every place" and "holy hands" mean (m2, m3).

decisions.choice: les hommes, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The word here means the male members of the church, set against the women of verse 9 (m1), so "les hommes" is meant as men and the inclusive setting does not apply.

source.text: ὡσαύτως καὶ γυναῖκας ἐν καταστολῇ κοσμίῳ μετὰ αἰδοῦς καὶ σωφροσύνης κοσμεῖν ἑαυτάς, μὴ ἐν πλέγμασιν καὶ χρυσίῳ ἢ μαργαρίταις ἢ ἱματισμῷ πολυτελεῖ, ἀλλ’ ὃ πρέπει γυναιξὶν ἐπαγγελλομέναις θεοσέβειαν, δι’ ἔργων ἀγαθῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Likewise also women in clothing respectable with modesty and self-control to adorn themselves, not with braided hair and gold or pearls or clothing expensive, \v 10 but what is fitting for women professing godliness, through works good.

en.L: Likewise also [I want] women to adorn themselves in respectable clothing, with modesty and self-control, not with braided hair and gold or pearls or expensive clothing, \v 10 but with what is fitting for women who profess godliness: with good works.
en.B: In the same way, I want women to dress in a fitting way, with modesty and good sense, and not to make braided hair, gold, pearls or costly clothes their adornment, \v 10 but good works, as is right for women who claim to honor God.
en.R: In the same way, women should wear clothes that are modest and sensible. They should not try to make themselves look beautiful with fancy hairstyles, gold jewelry, pearls or expensive clothes. \v 10 Women who say they love God should make themselves beautiful by doing good things.

fr.L: De même aussi, [je veux] que les femmes se parent d’une tenue convenable, avec pudeur et modération, non de cheveux tressés et d’or ou de perles ou de vêtements coûteux, \v 10 mais de ce qui convient à des femmes qui font profession de piété : d’œuvres bonnes.
fr.B: De même, je veux que les femmes s’habillent de manière convenable, avec pudeur et bon sens, et qu’elles ne fassent pas des cheveux tressés, de l’or, des perles ou des vêtements de prix leur parure, \v 10 mais des œuvres bonnes, comme il convient à des femmes qui déclarent honorer Dieu.
fr.R: De même, les femmes doivent porter des vêtements simples et convenables. Elles ne doivent pas chercher à se rendre belles avec des coiffures compliquées, des bijoux en or, des perles ou des vêtements chers. \v 10 Les femmes qui disent aimer Dieu doivent se rendre belles en faisant du bien.

decisions.choice: likewise: the same wish, perhaps also that the women pray
decisions.reason: ὡσαύτως ("likewise") carries over "I want" from verse 8, and may carry over "to pray" as well: women praying in a fitting manner (1 Corinthians 11:5).

decisions.choice: braided hair, gold, pearls, costly clothing: displays of wealth and status
decisions.reason: Elaborate hairstyles woven with gold and pearls were a mark of wealthy women in Roman cities, and moral writers of the time criticized them. 1 Peter 3:3-4 says the same.

decisions.choice: self-control: good sense, sound judgment
decisions.reason: σωφροσύνης is soundness of mind and self-restraint, a virtue for men and women alike in these letters (2:15; Titus 2:2-6).

decisions.choice: [I want]
decisions.reason: The verb carries over from verse 8 (m1).

decisions.choice: should make themselves beautiful by doing good things
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture of adornment.

source.text: γυνὴ ἐν ἡσυχίᾳ μανθανέτω ἐν πάσῃ ὑποταγῇ·

records.literal_gloss: A woman in quietness let learn in all submission;

en.L: Let a woman learn in quietness, in all submission.
en.B: A woman should learn quietly and with full submission.
en.R: Women should learn quietly, and they should accept what they are taught.

fr.L: Que la femme apprenne dans le calme, en toute soumission.
fr.B: La femme doit apprendre dans le calme et avec une entière soumission.
fr.R: Les femmes doivent apprendre dans le calme, et accepter ce qu’on leur enseigne.

decisions.choice: let a woman learn: a command that women be taught
decisions.reason: μανθανέτω is a command: women are to learn. In many settings of the time, women were not taught religious teaching.

decisions.choice: quietness: a calm, settled manner, not necessarily total silence
decisions.reason: ἡσυχίᾳ is the word used in verse 2 for a "quiet" life and in 2 Thessalonians 3:12; it describes a peaceable, undisturbed manner. Whether it means silence in the assembly or a quiet, receptive spirit is debated.

decisions.choice: in all submission: in full submission
decisions.reason: ὑποταγῇ is submission or subordination. The verse does not say to whom: to the teaching, to those who teach, or to husbands; readers differ.

decisions.choice: a woman: women in general, or wives
decisions.reason: γυνὴ can mean "woman" or "wife", and the word for man in verse 12 can mean "man" or "husband". The passage moves from women at prayer (verses 9-10) to Adam and Eve (verses 13-14), so it may concern women in the church or wives with their husbands.

decisions.choice: accept what they are taught
decisions.reason: Readable states one of the senses in m3, which the Greek leaves open.

decisions.choice: dans le calme (here and in verse 12)
decisions.reason: The word describes a calm, settled manner and need not mean total silence (m2), as the English "quietness" leaves open. "En silence" would decide the question; "dans le calme" keeps the wider sense.

source.text: διδάσκειν δὲ γυναικὶ οὐκ ἐπιτρέπω, οὐδὲ αὐθεντεῖν ἀνδρός, ἀλλ’ εἶναι ἐν ἡσυχίᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: To teach but a woman not I permit, nor to have authority over a man, but to be in quietness.

en.L: But I do not permit a woman to teach or to have authority over a man; rather, she is to be in quietness.
en.B: I do not allow a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man; she is to remain quiet.
en.R: I do not allow a woman to teach a man or to have authority over him. She should be quiet.

fr.L: Mais je ne permets pas à une femme d’enseigner, ni d’avoir autorité sur un homme ; elle doit plutôt être dans le calme.
fr.B: Je ne permets pas à une femme d’enseigner ni d’exercer l’autorité sur un homme ; elle doit se tenir dans le calme.
fr.R: Je ne permets pas à une femme d’enseigner un homme ni d’avoir autorité sur lui. Elle doit rester dans le calme.

decisions.choice: to have authority over: to exercise authority
alternatives: to assume authority on one's own initiative
decisions.reason: αὐθεντέω occurs only here in the New Testament and is rare elsewhere. In the writings that use it, it means to have or exercise authority, and sometimes to act in a high-handed or domineering way. Which sense it has here is one of the most debated questions in the letter.

decisions.choice: to teach or to have authority over a man: two things, or one
alternatives: one thing: to teach in a domineering way over a man
decisions.reason: οὐδὲ ("nor") may join two separate activities, teaching and exercising authority, or two that belong together; and "over a man" may go with both verbs or only with the second.

decisions.choice: I do not permit: Paul's present instruction
decisions.reason: ἐπιτρέπω is present tense, "I do not permit". The verse gives a reason in verses 13-14 drawn from creation and the fall. Whether it states a rule for all churches at all times or answers the situation in Ephesus, where false teachers were at work (1:3-7) and some women were drawn in (5:13-15; 2 Timothy 3:6-7), is a question of interpretation; the text itself does not settle it.

decisions.choice: to be in quietness
decisions.reason: The same word as in verse 11 (see the note there).

decisions.choice: to have authority over (L, R); to exercise authority over (B)
decisions.reason: The renderings follow the most common sense of the verb (m1), which is uncertain; the footnote gives the others.

decisions.choice: to teach a man
decisions.reason: Readable follows the reading in which "a man" goes with both verbs (m2), which is uncertain.

source.text: Ἀδὰμ γὰρ πρῶτος ἐπλάσθη, εἶτα Εὕα·

records.literal_gloss: Adam for first was formed, then Eve;

en.L: For Adam was formed first, then Eve.
en.B: For Adam was formed first, and then Eve.
en.R: God made Adam first, and then Eve.

fr.L: Car Adam a été formé le premier, puis Ève.
fr.B: Car Adam a été formé le premier, et Ève ensuite.
fr.R: Dieu a fait Adam en premier, et ensuite Ève.

decisions.choice: Adam formed first, then Eve: Genesis 2:7 and 2:21-22
decisions.reason: πλάσσω is the verb the Greek Old Testament uses in Genesis 2:7 for God forming the man. Paul gives the order of creation as a reason for what he has just said.

decisions.choice: God made
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the maker (Genesis 2).

source.text: καὶ Ἀδὰμ οὐκ ἠπατήθη, ἡ δὲ γυνὴ ἐξαπατηθεῖσα ἐν παραβάσει γέγονεν.

records.literal_gloss: and Adam not was deceived, the but woman having been deceived into transgression has come.

en.L: And Adam was not deceived, but the woman was deceived and came into transgression.
en.B: And Adam was not the one deceived; it was the woman who was deceived and fell into sin.
en.R: And Adam was not the one who was tricked. The woman was tricked, and she disobeyed God.

fr.L: Et Adam n’a pas été trompé, mais la femme, ayant été trompée, est tombée dans la transgression.
fr.B: Et ce n’est pas Adam qui a été trompé ; c’est la femme qui a été trompée et qui est tombée dans le péché.
fr.R: Et ce n’est pas Adam qui a été trompé. C’est la femme qui a été trompée, et elle a désobéi à Dieu.

decisions.choice: the woman was deceived: Genesis 3:13
decisions.reason: Eve said, "The serpent deceived me" (Genesis 3:13). Paul does not say Adam was innocent: elsewhere it is through Adam that sin entered the world (Romans 5:12-19). Here the point is who was deceived; how the verse supports verse 12 is read in different ways.

decisions.choice: tricked
decisions.reason: Plainer words.

source.text: σωθήσεται δὲ διὰ τῆς τεκνογονίας, ἐὰν μείνωσιν ἐν πίστει καὶ ἀγάπῃ καὶ ἁγιασμῷ μετὰ σωφροσύνης.

records.literal_gloss: She will be saved but through the childbearing, if they continue in faith and love and holiness with self-control.

en.L: But she will be saved through childbearing, if they continue in faith and love and holiness with self-control.
en.B: Yet she will be saved through childbearing, if they continue in faith, love and holiness, with self-control.
en.R: But women will be saved through childbearing, if they keep on living with faith, love and holiness, and with self-control.

fr.L: Mais elle sera sauvée par l’enfantement, si elles demeurent dans la foi, l’amour et la sainteté, avec modération.
fr.B: Cependant, elle sera sauvée en donnant naissance à des enfants, si elles persévèrent dans la foi, l’amour et la sainteté, avec bon sens.
fr.R: Mais les femmes seront sauvées en mettant des enfants au monde, si elles continuent à vivre avec foi, amour et sainteté, et avec bon sens.

decisions.choice: saved through childbearing
alternatives: kept safe through the dangers of childbirth
saved through "the childbearing": the birth of the promised child, Christ (Genesis 3:15)
saved while living out her calling as wife and mother
decisions.reason: σῴζω elsewhere in these letters means salvation in Christ (2:4), and the condition that follows ("if they continue in faith") points the same way. τεκνογονίας is childbearing; with the article it may mean childbirth in general or a particular birth. Readers take the verse as saying that women are saved, not by teaching or authority, in the ordinary life of a woman of that time, or kept safe in childbirth, or saved through the birth of the Messiah promised in Genesis 3:15. The verse is among the most disputed in the letter.

decisions.choice: she ... they: the woman (Eve and women after her), then women in general
alternatives: they: the woman and her husband
decisions.reason: σωθήσεται ("she will be saved") is singular, picking up "the woman" of verse 14; μείνωσιν ("they continue") is plural, most likely women in general.

decisions.choice: self-control: good sense

decisions.choice: si elles demeurent (L); si elles persévèrent (B)
decisions.reason: The English "they" has no gender, but French must give one. Following m2, "they" are women in general, after "she" (Eve and the women after her), so French writes the feminine "elles". "Ils" would suggest the husbands or the children, a reading the meaning decision does not take.
